These models capture basic steady-state and dynamic load characteristics. 3.3.2 Additional Model Requirements For data center applications, custom models should address: 10 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. • Fast transient behavior associated with AI-driven workload fluctuations • Power demand diversity reflecting heterogeneous server types (central processing units, graphics processing units) • Interaction effects with cooling and environmental systems to simulate coupled demand changes • Support for real-time adaptive load control mechanisms for grid support functions. 3.4 Uninterruptible Power Supply UPS models must accurately capture: • Dual-mode operation—grid-following during normal operation and grid-forming during islanded or backup modes • Transition logic for seamless switching between utility power and battery backup in response to faults or power quality events • Compliance with ride-through requirements during voltage disturbances. 3.4.1 Standard PSCAD Models Available PSCAD does not include specific UPS library components. Common practice is to represent UPS units either as ideal voltage sources or by building custom inverter models with integrated battery systems. 3.4.2 Additional Model Requirements Custom UPS inverter and battery management system models are required to emulate real UPS behavior during dynamic load changes, battery charge/discharge cycles, and power quality events. Integration with data center energy management systems and coordination with BESS are necessary for the accurate simulation of backup power architectures in data centers. 3.5 Cooling Loads Cooling load models must encompass: • Voltage and frequency sensitivity of motor-driven components, such as pumps and fans • Control logic for staged startup, load shedding, and curtailment during grid events or demand response • Thermal inertia effects influencing cooling system recovery times after disturbances • Coordination with facility management systems to reflect realistic operational sequences. 3.5.1 Standard PSCAD Models Available PSCAD includes generic motor load components that can be used to model variable-frequency drive-driven pumps, chillers, and fans commonly found in cooling systems. 3.5.2 Additional Model Requirements Customized models should be developed to: • Capture detailed variable-frequency drive control schemes and their dynamic response to grid disturbances. 11 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. • Model interactions between cooling loads and IT loads, including common medium- voltage bus influences. • Represent emergency backup operation modes powered by UPS or generators. • Support integration with data center energy management and supervisory control systems for demand flexibility and resilience strategies. 3.6 Battery Energy Storage System BESS models must comprehensively capture: • Fast transient response and dynamic control during grid events, including seamless operation in both grid-connected and island modes • Performance criteria outlined in the Institute for Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) Std 1547 (IEEE 2018), such as autonomous frequency response, voltage support, and disturbance ride-through • Accurate battery state-of-charge management and interactions with site controllers, especially under rapid load changes. 3.6.1 Standard PSCAD Models Available PSCAD includes generic battery storage models and inverter-based templates that simulate charge/discharge cycles, grid-following and grid-forming controls, and interactions with AC/DC systems.
